fields.heading:
The Hands
of Worcester.
fields.intro: A community-led public art installation by Jessica Mary Monk, made in conjunction with The Worcester Plinth. 211 people took part.
fields.summary: Workshops across Worcester earlier this year collected plaster casts of people’s hands. The casts were painted, sealed in resin and mounted, and sit atop The Worcester Plinth, a plinth that moves from location to location within Worcester, for 9 months.
fields.concept: The human hand is unique to every individual on this earth. From unique fingerprints used to identify us, to hands who hold each other, the human experience is informed by touch. Hands create, they comfort, they tell a story. As a human race we have always had a fascination with hands, from cave paintings dating 40,000 years ago of hand prints, to hands in art; hands gesture and contain our stories, our histories and our emotions. As children are held by their mothers; as we are held by each other.
fields.artist_statement: The Hands of Worcester is a community led project, I wanted to get out into the community and take a historical cast of the communities hands at that time. Now it is displayed before you, I hope you can see the unique and magical quality as I did when I made each and every cast. A thank you to the project team as a whole and especially to my husband, Guy, who helped and supported the whole process.
fields.community: 211 people took part. The youngest participant was 5 months old and the oldest was 90. Thank you to every participant.
fields.making: Plaster casts were taken in workshops across Worcester, then painted, sealed in resin and mounted on the plinth. Jessica also made charcoal and acrylic studies of hands alongside the installation. Photographs of those studies have not been added yet.
fields.exhibition: The hands sit on The Worcester Plinth for 9 months. The plinth moves from location to location within Worcester.
fields.funding: Supported using public funding by the National Lottery through Arts Council England. With thanks to funders and supporters, including The Elmley Foundation.
fields.seo_description: 211 people took part. Community-led public art by Jessica Mary Monk with The Worcester Plinth, on show for 9 months. The names shown are those who agreed to be shown.
